attributes.nuance_translation: A phrase used when (A) is being given from the speaker, or someone in their in-group, to somebody else.

attributes.body:
あげる is a verb with many uses in Japanese. It's original meaning is 'to raise', but is also used as a polite speech way of saying 'to give'. In this way it can be thought of as similar to 'to offer up' in English. As polite speech has the same basic subject and object rules as standard speech, the giver will be marked with は or が, while the recipient will be marked with に. As usual, the 'object' that is being given will be marked with を.

From these three examples, we can see that the order of 'giver', 'recipient', and 'object' does not matter, so long as the correct particles are used.

Caution

あげる should not be used when giving something to someone of a higher status, or when lowering oneself to elevate another. This is done through honorific language, or humble speech, and will use different verbs.

Fun Fact

Although あげる is considered polite speech, it is the most natural way of saying 'to give'. やる is the 'casual' equivalent of あげる, but due to やる sounding a little bit rough, あげる became the standard.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Inner/outer circles and which verb to use
あげる, くれる, and もらう as Verbs

attributes.body: あげる and くれる are basic verbs for giving. あげる is used when the speaker or their in-group gives something to someone outside the group, or when one out-group member gives to another. くれる is used when someone outside the speaker's group gives something to the speaker or their in-group. In both cases, the subject marked by が is the giver.

first_relatable.title: あげる
first_relatable.meaning: To give (away), To present, To provide

attributes.body: あげる means 'to give' and is used when the speaker or someone in their in-group gives something to someone outside the group. The subject, marked by が, is the giver. In contrast, もらう means 'to receive' and describes the act from the receiver's perspective. With もらう, the subject marked by が is the one receiving.

first_relatable.title: もらう
first_relatable.meaning: To receive, To get, To obtain

second_relatable.title: あげる
second_relatable.meaning: To give (away), To present, To provide

attributes.body: あげる is a basic verb meaning 'to give,' often used when the giver is the speaker or someone in the speaker's in-group, and the receiver is outside that group. For example, プレゼントをあげる means 'to give a present.' When used as てあげる after a verb in the て form, it means doing something for someone's benefit. For example, 英語を教えてあげる means 'to teach English (to someone as a favor).'

first_relatable.title: あげる
first_relatable.meaning: To give (away), To present, To provide

second_relatable.title: てあげる
second_relatable.meaning: To do something for someone, As a favor for
